title: Surgical traffic reroute and KV-cache desync patch for asymmetric inter-region routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-severity customer escalations reported 2026-03-01 after sustained 5–15% error rates for a subset of requests in Hosted and Dedicated tenants. Root cause traced to asymmetric routing between regions that caused inconsistent KV-cache warmings and stale cache lookups during cross-region failovers. This ticket captures a minimally invasive traffic reroute ("surgical reroute"), a corrective runtime patch to make KV-cache validation tolerant, and a customer communication/rollback plan.
background: At ~2026-03-01T10:42Z multiple Dedicated customers reported elevated 5xx errors and latency spikes when their traffic was routed through Region-B with fallback to Region-A. Investigation showed uneven prefix steering and occasional request replays across different model-serving pools resulting in divergent in-memory KV-cache state. Existing cache validation assumed monotonic routing within a session and failed to recover when requests were split across regions.
impact_summary: Impacted: ~12 Dedicated tenants (low volume) + ~3 Hosted customers; symptom: 5–15% increased 5xxs and duplicated tokens in outputs; duration: intermittent over 4 hours before mitigation. Business impact: degraded SLAs for a small cohort and multiple urgent customer escalations requiring on-call intervention.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate session with primary in region-A and a transient failover to region-B mid-session. 2) Warm prefix cache from region-A. 3) Replay requests routed to region-B without corresponding prefix warming. 4) Observe stale KV-cache key mismatches and error class X-ERR-KV-MISALIGN.
immediate_actions: Opened customer-facing incident updates and flagged Dedicated tenants with SRE/AMs
Applied rate-limited surgical reroute to prevent cross-region mid-session splits for affected tenants (see traffic_reroute_steps)
Enabled additional request-level cache validation logging at debug for 2 hours for correlation
Notified network and infra teams; created BGP/community steering audit ticket
mitigation_workaround: For affected Dedicated tenants we enforced single-region sticky routing at the load-balancer level for session duration (30m) to avoid cross-region cache divergence. For Hosted customers we temporarily disabled aggressive failover for non-critical models until patch landed.
traffic_reroute_steps: Identify tenant prefixes with >3 errors in 15m window using routing-dashboard query 'tenant_errors>3'
Apply sticky routing flag on edge-proxy for tenant: curl -XPOST https://api.edge.internal/tenants/{tenant_id}/stickiness -d '{"duration":1800, "region": "region-A"}'
Confirm connections drain: monitor 'active_sessions' metric; wait until <5 sessions transition for region-B
Gradually re-open routing with 5% traffic shadowing after patch verification
hotfix_pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512 - kv-cache: tolerate out-of-order prefix warmings and add conservative reconciliation step
rollback_plan: If hotfix shows regressions, revert edge stickiness by removing tenant stickiness flags and restore standard failover; apply temporary routing filter that sends only control-plane traffic across regions until a full patch is validated. Expected rollback time <= 30 minutes.
timeline: 2026-03-01T10:42Z - first customer alert; 11:05Z - triage; 11:30Z - surgical reroute applied for top 6 tenants; 12:00Z - debug logs enabled and PR opened; 2026-03-02 - hotfix landed to staging; 2026-03-04 - staging verification; 2026-03-05 - canary rollout to 2 tenants; ongoing: monitoring & communications

2026-03-01 13:00 UTC - Customer-facing status posted to status.redwood.ai
